prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1084; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant after a hit while turning left at an intersection. The claimant states the other vehicle struck the side of their car as they turned across oncoming traffic. Claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the account, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle. Damage to the driver side matches the impact described by the claimant. A few older scratches are present in the same area and may predate this crash, so they have been noted separately for the estimate.

Entry 5: Claimant reported a wrist fracture. The injury is consistent with the type of impact described and is plausible for a crash of this kind. No prior injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 6: Medical records show treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant later added a few small details to the account, but the core description of the collision has remained the same across each statement.

Entry 7: Based on the policy confirmation, scene photos, police information, vehicle inspection, and medical records, the claim is proceeding under standard review. Next step is to finalize the repair estimate and the injury evaluation.
